title: Quantifying the fidelity of a quantum memory
authors: Victor Barizien, Sophie Egelhaaf, Angelo Gelmini Rodriguez, Louis Nicolas, Théo Sanchez Mejia, Mikael Afzelius, Pavel Sekatski, Nicolas Brunner
abstract: Quantum memories are key ingredients for future quantum networks. Developing methods for their certification is therefore an important, yet challenging, problem. In this work, we present a general framework for certifying quantum memories and quantifying their performance in an operational and efficient manner, taking advantage of developments in the theory of quantum channels. We start by giving a pedagogical introduction to these concepts and tools and illustrate their natural application to quantum memories. Specifically, we quantify the fidelity of a quantum memory via the notion of average channel fidelity, which can be estimated precisely in an experiment via a finite set of probe states forming a so-called $2$-design. We then present a number of witnessing techniques for certifying this quantity, and show that it gives access to other important properties of the channel, such as its dimensionality and its capacity to transmit quantum information. We consider mostly a simple prepare-and-measure scenario, but discuss also the case of an entanglement-based setup, as well as a semi-device-independent approach. Finally, we apply these methods to a solid-state quantum memory experiment, certifying an average channel fidelity of 98.6%. Our certification methods can be readily applied to other quantum devices, such as fibers, transducers and gates.
summary: This work establishes a comprehensive framework to certify the performance of quantum memories by quantifying their average channel fidelity. The authors utilize methods based on 2-designs and entanglement testing, which allow for precise estimation from limited experimental measurements. The framework is successfully applied to solid-state quantum memory, achieving a high fidelity certification of 98.6%.
main_problem: The paper develops a general, operational, and efficient framework for certifying the performance and quantifying the fidelity of quantum memories.
main_result: The authors successfully certified an average channel fidelity of 98.6% for a solid-state quantum memory experiment, demonstrating the framework's practical utility.
method: They quantify fidelity using the average channel fidelity, estimated via a 2-design formed by a finite set of probe states, and also using entanglement-based and semi-device-independent techniques.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a quantum memory, treated mathematically as a quantum channel $M$ mapping input states to output states. The ideal memory is the identity channel.
key_observables: Average channel fidelity ($F_{	ext{avg}}$), Choi fidelity ($F_{	ext{CJ}}$), and average efficiency ($\eta(M)$).
important_parameters: Storage time (e.g., $10 \mu	ext{s}$ or $125 \mu	ext{s}$), dimensionality ($d$), and the number of probe states used in the 2-design.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is replacing the integral over all pure states (Haar measure) with an estimate derived from a finite set of probe states forming a 2-design.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates estimating $F_{	ext{avg}}$ for a qubit memory using prepare-and-measure setups with varying numbers of probe states (2, 4, or 6).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the framework, details the 2-design estimation for prepare-and-measure scenarios, discusses entanglement-based and semi-device-independent testing, and concludes with applications to solid-state memory experiments.
why_interesting: The rigorous quantification of memory fidelity using established quantum information tools (like 2-designs and Choi fidelity) provides a direct, measurable benchmark for quantum hardware development.

FIG. 3. Lower bound on the average channel fidelity Favg(M, id) of a qubit memory M as a function of the witness value T{Ψx} using 2, 4 and 6 states (respectively in green, or- ange and blue). For the 6-state witness, the quantity T{Ψx} corresponds to Favg. The 4- and 2-state protocols provide lower bounds on Favg, which are computed via an SDP opti- miasation, as described in Appendix B. Certifying a fidelity Favg > 2/3 ensures that the channel is not entanglement- breaking, while Favg > 1/2 guarantees the channel is not correlation-breaking.

A lower bound on the single-letter quantum channel capacity Q(1)(M) normalized by the ideal value log(d), as a function of the Choi-Jamio lkowski fidelity of the channel FCJ(M, id), in dimension d = 2, 3, 4, 5 (from bottom to top). The numerical values give the threshold fidelity below which no positive quantum capacity is guaranteed.

FIG. 5. Semi-device-independent scenario for certifying the quantum memory. The preparation device is assumed to be trusted, i.e. upon receiving the classical input x, the de- vice produces the state Ψx which is then stored in the quan- tum memory M. The output state of the memory is then measured through a device which is a priori uncharacterized, where y denotes the measurement choice and b its outcome. From the observed statistics, p(b|ψx, y), one can lower bound the average channel fidelity of the quantum memory.
